Sovereign Federation Lab / Reader guide · edition 09

An entity directory is not a relocation switch.

Bind entities to approved physical stores, then evaluate every candidate crossing against that binding.

The synthetic container lab is validated. Technical extension points on this page remain proposals unless explicitly identified as implemented. Understand the labels.

Migration impact and execution

The prototype calculates entity eligibility and affected customer conflicts for a proposed store. It does not write to the directory. A production migration must protect both owner records and inbound projections, with placement-version permits, old-writer fencing and policy reconciliation. A customer exclusion can veto a move that is otherwise acceptable to the legal entity.

No thirty-cluster assumption

Use a store per required physical/operational boundary, not necessarily per legal entity. Shared stores save infrastructure but require strong entity authorization and isolation. Add actual country stores where rules cannot be met by the current three hubs.

For implementers: engineering brief
HAND OFF TO ENGINEERING

A focused prompt with scope, contracts and acceptance criteria.

Read the full prompt
Entity relocation decision: keep legal entity identity stable while changing physical home. Use a lawful transition policy, snapshot plus continuous change capture, versioned tombstones, target-applied checkpoints, graph closure and an entity-specific source writer fence. Persist source fencing before activating the target; never flip routing back after target writes. Separate placement version, writer epoch, policy revision and resource data version. Migration consumes the capped bulk lane; guard and operational capacity remain reserved. The executable edition-08 slice uses isolated mig_* row envelopes and one coordinator; it does not migrate the original normalized business.* fixture or prove distributed fencing. Read Entity relocation before implementation.

Build signed, versioned entity/store registries and a read-only impact planner first. Then implement a reviewed migration state machine with gates for entity policy, customer exclusions, owner fencing, projection reconciliation and rollback. Test failure at every step. No PATCH store_id shortcut and no implicit nearest-store fallback.
